visualMethod.observations: No clipped name, date, missing page, overlapped writing, filled signature, completed notarization, marked judicial disposition or invented service certification observed. All blank sworn fact boxes remain unmarked. Custom orders are expressly identified as participant-prepared, not official court forms. Internal route identifiers and copied registry prose are verbose but readable; verbosity is not counted as a visual failure.

rows.positiveFindings: Part Two and ten-year felony treatment are identified. The inherited five-year exclusion sentence is expressly warned against, so it is not treated as an undisclosed timing error. Superior no-filing-fee language on page 10 is independently corroborated. The false official-order source requirement stays retired.

DC-33 Part Three A, five-year sentence-completion wait and conviction-court destination are consistently identified. No conviction or sworn eligibility fact is pre-attested. The no-fee paragraph does not silently apply the Superior FAQ to a District filing.

Superior-55 Part Three, the written deferral agreement, completion and compliance hearing, no additional completion-to-filing wait, and protected court findings are identified. The full-payment condition on this deferred route is not treated as the same error as the first-offender waiver omission.

DC-33 Part Three B, ten years from the last sentence, no felony, and the statutory domestic-violence/DUI/refusal exclusions are disclosed. The inconsistent printed six-conviction affidavit is preserved rather than silently edited. It does not justify manufacturing uncertainty about the statute's two-through-five threshold.

findings.finding: The required BCI acquisition step tells the participant to request a criminal history but does not identify the expungement-purpose request or give its current practical acquisition requirements and separate cost. An ordinary public/employment BCI omits some matters relevant to the packet's own arrest/history checks.
findings.repair: Give the official BCI purpose-specific instructions: tell BCI the report is for expungement; provide the current official acquisition link, $5 state-check cost distinct from a filing fee, valid photo-ID requirement and actual in-person or mail procedure. Do not imply that an ordinary clean state report proves no relevant arrest history. Keep signatures/releases participant-executed. Do not substitute a $45 employment national-fingerprint workflow.
findings.regression: Both fixture guides include the expungement purpose and distinct state-check cost; neither claims a generic clean report proves eligibility. Verify any added acquisition component and protected fields. This is a source-backed instruction repair, not a new counsel decision.

findings.finding: The final participant-authored certified-copy checklist categorically tells the participant to pay everything in full, although earlier route guidance correctly recognizes court-approved reduction or waiver. Quoting the official form's short instruction does not cure the contradictory added command.
findings.repair: Preserve the official form. Make the added checklist follow the actual court order and balances legally remaining after any approved reduction or waiver; do not say all original sums must be paid notwithstanding that order. Distinguish restitution from remittable costs and fines. No participant may self-declare an obligation waived.
findings.regression: A fixture with an actual approved costs/fines waiver does not receive an unconditional instruction to pay the waived amount. A fixture without an order cannot assume a waiver. Do not apply this correction indiscriminately to the deferred-sentence route.

findings.finding: Both page-12 self-help-stop lists import a rule stopping for any prior conviction or probation because it defeats first-offender status. That is not the eligibility structure of these two routes. Deferred guidance also imports an undefined first-offender lookback despite correctly stating immediate post-completion consideration earlier.
findings.repair: Replace the copied first-offender stops with each route's own conditions. Multiple misdemeanors must not stop merely because the person has the additional misdemeanor convictions the route exists to address. Deferred must use agreement compliance, the statutory hearing conditions, no pending proceeding and the violence exclusion, not an invented additional first-offender wait. Preserve actual contested-fact and professional-help boundaries.
findings.regression: Eligible two-through-five misdemeanor scenarios are not categorically stopped as non-first-offenders. A completed compliant deferred-sentence scenario is not given a new five/ten-year waiting period or categorical prior-misdemeanor bar. Disqualifying actual route facts still stop the route.

findings.finding: Current DC-33 instructions say fewer than six, while its affidavit says not more than six. Current section 12-1.3-2(b) expressly permits more than one but fewer than six and allows any or all of those misdemeanors. The added guide nevertheless says whether fewer than six means up to five is unresolved.
findings.repair: State the ordinary statutory threshold as two through five misdemeanor convictions, with no felony and the other subsection conditions. Six does not become eligible because of the affidavit wording. Count the relevant convictions, not merely the subset selected for this motion. Keep edge cases such as reclassification, previously cleared matters or disputed history separately escalated rather than declaring simple integer arithmetic a legal hold. Do not alter the official affidavit or pre-attest its boxes.
findings.regression: Test ordinary histories with one, two, five and six misdemeanors. Two/five are not rejected just for the count; six is not admitted through the form discrepancy; one goes to the appropriate distinct route. Other eligibility conditions remain operative.

findings.resolution: The statutory mechanism is chapter 12-1.3 expungement after the section 12-19-19(c) compliance hearing, not the separate identification-record destruction route. The second motion relief bullet is the chapter-12-1.3 expungement request and is consistent with that mechanism. Remove the broad unresolved-mechanism claim after A adopts this source-backed resolution; do not invent an extra conviction requirement or automatically switch to the first sealing/destruction bullet.
findings.limit: This does not claim that a clerk approved a particular filing or that counsel reviewed the custom proposed order. The owner's exact-output commercial gate remains separate.

findings.finding: Current official Superior-55, revised February 2025, still uses single felony on its instruction page and single misdemeanor in Part Two's sworn statement. This session independently saw both in the currently published official PDF. The packet correctly leaves the box unmarked and warns against an untrue oath.
findings.exactRemainingQuestion: What corrected affidavit text, attachment, or acknowledged court-approved handling should a felony filer use for this particular sworn statement? Obtain an issuer correction or actual qualified legal determination. Do not ask again whether an ordinary first-offender felony uses the ten-year statutory route.
findings.commercialEffect: No permission to swear a false misdemeanor statement; no fabricated clerk response.

findings.finding: The Superior Court FAQ affirmatively says no expungement fee. It has now been directly checked instead of merely owner-relayed. It is not, by itself, an independently verified District Court filing-fee schedule. Current section 12-1.3-3(c) contains no former $100 grant charge. Two attempts to read the full 2021 chapter-141 enactment timed out; its search excerpt and a pre-enactment AG press release are not labeled as a fetched and hashed enacted text.
findings.exactRemainingQuestion: For these District Court filings, confirm the present filing charge, if any, from a District-specific official source or actual clerk response. Do not reintroduce the repealed $100 grant charge, apply civil fees, or ask counsel to find a nonexistent official proposed-order form.
